status.label: Investigate updater failure/recovery state
status.detail: Supplied archives and contradictory up-to-date/error UI require error classification and state-transition testing, not a generic network diagnosis.

next_action.label: Reproduce update error then successful recovery
next_action.reason: Separate real transport errors, metadata failures and stale UI state.

judgment.rationale: The long-running report includes repeated update failures, multiple archives and a screenshot of successful/up-to-date state alongside a red network error. VPN recovery for one user does not establish a universal network cause.
evidence: The report spans 0.66 through 0.79 and contains twelve comments and already-supplied diagnostics.
One commenter reports VPN-dependent success; another recovers hours later.
A follow-up shows green up-to-date and red network-error indicators simultaneously.
common/updating/updating.cpp get_github_version_info_async catches request, JSON parsing and asset extraction exceptions together and returns NETWORK_ERROR.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce controlled failure/recovery and inspect the updater-to-Settings state contract; preserve actual network failures rather than assuming all reports are cosmetic.

fix_assessment.rationale: A bounded updater result/state correction is applicable; no targeted linked fix proves that all historical transport failures are handled.

proposed_fixes.title: Differentiate update failures and clear obsolete error state
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The inspected backend maps several exception classes to NETWORK_ERROR. The simultaneous success/error display suggests an obsolete error can outlive a later successful result, but that UI transition and the original transport failures remain unconfirmed.
plan: Add controlled request-failure, malformed-release metadata, missing-asset and successful-recovery cases around the update-check result boundary.
Trace how each result reaches Settings and identify whether stale or overlapping attempts leave contradictory flags.
Separate supported transport and metadata failure categories without exposing secrets; clear obsolete error state only when the same or newer successful attempt is committed.
Preserve retry behavior, release-channel selection and legitimate failure visibility; do not alter proxy/TLS security or recommend VPN as a product fix.
Add a regression that renders the failure-to-up-to-date transition without contradictory status indicators.
verification: Fail then succeed and confirm the visible state represents the latest completed check.
Malformed metadata and missing installer assets are distinguishable from transport failures.
Stable/prerelease and available-update/up-to-date paths continue to work.

confidence.rationale: The catch-all backend result is directly verified and the contradictory screenshot narrows a state test; neither the frontend transition nor the original failures' common cause has been traced.

issue_context.summary: The updater reports a generic network error across several releases; later evidence also shows success and failure simultaneously.
known_information: Multiple diagnostic ZIPs are already present.
Network/environment changes helped some users but not all.
Backend request, parse and asset failures currently share a generic NETWORK_ERROR outcome.
inferences: The issue may combine genuine transient connectivity failures with misleading/stale presentation; these should not be collapsed into one asserted root cause.
issue_context.analysis: The public evidence is adequate for maintainer-side failure/recovery tests. Another generic log request would not resolve the confirmed backend classification ambiguity or the UI state contract.
initial_investigation: Read the body, all twelve comments and linked-work timeline.
Inspected get_github_version_info_async and its request/parse/asset-extraction catch boundary.
Compared the VPN, delayed-recovery and contradictory-status observations.

actions.label: Review updater failure/recovery plan
actions.description: Approve the bounded classification/state investigation rather than an assumed network-access fix.

prerequisites: Use a development build with real version-check behavior enabled; 0.0 development versions skip checks.
Provide an isolated test seam for HTTP results and release metadata; do not disable certificate validation on an installed user build.
steps: Run a successful up-to-date check and record the Settings status.
Inject a transport failure and verify a single accurate failure state.
Restore a successful response and verify the old error clears.
Repeat with malformed JSON, missing installer asset and overlapping checks; compare result order with displayed state.
reproduce.expected_result: Settings shows a coherent current result, and distinct backend failure categories remain diagnosable.
reproduce.setup_prompt: Prepare deterministic updater response fixtures for transport failure, malformed JSON, valid up-to-date metadata and a newer release missing its expected installer asset. Drive the actual backend-to-Settings result path without changing production network security.
